drafts.title: Supercharger Waitlist at 300 US sites, 3 minutes to plug in
drafts.angle: No more circling the lot guessing who's next. The car holds your place in line now, right before the busiest charging week of the year. He RT'd the pilot on Nov 19; this is the 300-site rollout and his own Thanksgiving stops, not a repeat.
bullets: Tesla turned on Supercharger Waitlist at 300 US sites (announced Nov 19). The pilot started in May at 5 sites in CA and NY.
Join from the Tesla app (v4.62.3 or newer) or the touchscreen (software 2026.38 or newer). Navigating to the site in a Tesla can add you automatically as you get close.
When it's your turn you get a stall and 3 minutes to plug in, with an option to add 30 seconds. Tapping Can't Charge on a blocked stall keeps your turn.
Older Tegra-screen Teslas use the app. Non-Tesla EVs can join through the Tesla app too.

drafts.title: Europe makes fast chargers take a plain bank card by Jan 1
drafts.angle: Europe says fast chargers have to take a regular bank card, no app. We should want the same here. Different from Nov 19 Plug & Charge (auto pay): this is the card reader as the universal backup.
bullets: EU AFIR rule (Regulation 2023/1804): new public chargers since Apr 13, 2024 must allow ad hoc payment with no contract or sign-up.
Chargers 50 kW and up can't rely on a QR code alone. They need a card reader or contactless terminal.
Starting Jan 1, 2027 the rule reaches existing high-power chargers on major routes too.
US: no federal card-reader rule for every charger, and most networks still push their own app.
drafts.body: Europe's making fast chargers take a plain bank card by Jan 1. No app. My best stop this month was {$0.10 per kWh at IONNA Fruita} on an app, but I've got {how many charging apps are on my phone} on my phone. Should US chargers take tap-to-pay like a gas pump?
drafts.framework_body:
Europe's making fast chargers take a plain bank card by Jan 1.

No app. No account. Tap and charge, like a gas pump. New chargers there already had to do it, and starting Jan 1 the big highway ones have to catch up.

Here I've got {how many charging apps are on my phone} on my phone. My IONNA stop in Fruita was {$0.10 per kWh} and the app worked great. Not every app does.

{who in my life won't download a charging app}

Apps are fine. A card reader should be the backup everywhere.

Should US chargers have to take a tap-to-pay card?

drafts.title: Buying solar in 2026? The 30% credit is gone if you own it
drafts.angle: The tax break flipped. Leases still get it, owners don't. Know which deal you're being sold before you sign.
bullets: The federal 30% residential clean energy credit (25D) ended for homeowner-owned systems installed after 2025 (IRS).
Leased or third-party-owned systems can still use the business credit through the installer (Solar Power World, Nov 16).
Some installers say owning is still the better long-run deal; leases can cost more over 25 years.
Get at least two quotes and read transfer terms before signing (Michigan AG consumer warning, Nov 10).

drafts.title: $2.61 a month back: Rhode Island's wind contracts flip to a bill credit
drafts.angle: A charge on the bill flips to a credit. That's what wind looks like when it actually shows up on the statement. Keep it bill-focused, no climate talk.
bullets: Rhode Island Energy filed Nov 13 to turn a 0.353-cent/kWh renewable-contract charge into a 0.148-cent credit starting Jan 1, 2027.
Typical 500 kWh home: $179.97 down to $177.36 a month, which is $2.61 less.
Revolution Wind is among the contracts covered.
Still needs PUC approval (Docket 26-51-EL).
drafts.body: $2.61 a month back. Rhode Island's wind contracts are about to show up as a credit on the electric bill instead of a charge. Small, but it's real money. {what I'd like to see on my Xcel bill} Would you notice $2.61?
drafts.framework_body:
$2.61 a month back.

Rhode Island's wind contracts used to be a charge on the electric bill. Starting in January, if regulators sign off, they flip to a credit. A typical home goes from $179.97 to $177.36.

Small. But it's the first time I've seen wind show up as money back on the statement.
